description:
Magic Patterns (W23) is one of the fastest-growing design tools in AI, helping product teams turn ideas into interactive, code-backed prototypes in minutes.

Alex Danilowicz and his co-founder, both front-end engineers, built Magic Patterns to solve a problem they had themselves: finding a better way to turn ideas into something visual. They were among the first teams building prompt-to-design tools back in 2023.

In this episode of Design Review, Alex joins YC’s Aaron Epstein to demo Magic Patterns and its new MagicOS canvas, where teams can bring together prompts, images, PRDs, and other context to explore ideas visually. Then they review a handful of startup websites to break down what makes a site feel “vibe coded,” where founders go wrong, and how to make AI-generated design feel more intentional.

Chapters:
01:00 — What is Magic Patterns?
02:11 — From YC Pivot to Product-Market Fit
03:44 — Staying Ahead as AI Design Tools Improve
04:37 — Demo: Designing With Magic Patterns
09:52 — MagicOS
11:23 — Designing With Context on a Canvas
14:50 — How to Get Better Results From AI Design Tools
15:35 — How Far Can AI-Generated Design Go?
18:17 — Website Review 1: Ego
23:59 — Website Review 2: Sentient OS
32:01 — Website Review 3: Cerenovus
36:59 — Website Review 4: Slashy
43:33 — How to Develop Better Design Taste
44:20 — Why Everyone at Magic Patterns Talks to Users
45:07 — Balancing Speed and Design Quality
46:07 — The Future of Design and Magic Patterns
